needs_review.issue: Spouse named only in body text — not in slug and not in page title
needs_review.finding: A recurring FOCUS shape sits between the BRIEF's shape 1 and shape 2: the page is plainly a married-couple/family page and the snippet names the spouse, but the slug names only the missionary and the TITLE names only the missionary. Per the BRIEF grading table ('neither the slug nor the title names them → do not emit') these spouses were withheld. Affected pages and the body-only spouse first names: /missionaries/joshua-funderburk/ (Lindsay), /missionaries/bremerkamps/ (Maria), /missionaries/mark-joseph-family/ (Amy), /missionaries/ryan-brisnehan/ (Abby), /missionaries/timothy-broderick/ (Emily), /missionaries/mary-grace-matson/ (Blake), /missionaries/kallin-hill/ (Stephen, himself described as a FOCUS senior financial analyst), /missionaries/alice-ayers/ (Matthew, surname not stated).
needs_review.evidence: Search snippets, e.g. 'Josh Funderburk and his wife Lindsay are serving as FOCUS Parish Missionaries at Christ The King in Tulsa'; 'Adam and Maria Bremerkamp serve as FOCUS Parish Missionaries'; 'Mark and Amy Joseph, along with Nathan, Elizabeth, Clara and Miriam'. In each case the indexed <title> shows only the one name.
needs_review.recommendation: Eight likely Tier A adults are being left on the table by the slug/title-only rule. Since page fetching was blocked here, a reviewer with fetch access should open these eight URLs and confirm the spouse is an adult FOCUS missionary rather than a relative, then admit them against the same source_url. If this shape is common site-wide, consider a third grading row in the next brief: 'spouse named in body as wife/husband on a shared family giving page'.

needs_review.finding: One snippet rendered as 'Eric, Teressa, and Anastasia Macsay are FOCUS missionaries who serve students at the University of Northern Iowa'. Anastasia is listed in the same series as the two adults, which reads like a third missionary, but the page TITLE is 'Eric and Teressa Macsay' — implying Anastasia is a child.
needs_review.evidence: https://focus.org/missionaries/macsay/ — title 'Eric and Teressa Macsay'; body snippet naming a third Macsay.
needs_review.recommendation: Withheld per the children rule (title names only two adults). Do not admit Anastasia Macsay without a fetch confirming she is an adult staff member.

needs_review.issue: First name published as initials only
needs_review.finding: /missionaries/jj-nazzaro/ is titled 'JJ Nazzaro'. The surname is published in full and the slug carries it, so this is not an agency anonymization (unlike the SEND/Converge initial-slug pattern the standing rules cover) — it appears to be a personal nickname. Withheld from people[] anyway because no given name is available.
needs_review.recommendation: Admit as 'JJ Nazzaro' if the CRM tolerates a nickname first name; otherwise leave withheld. This is a real, publicly named FOCUS missionary, not a protected worker.

needs_review.issue: Named FOCUS leaders with spouses but no citable /missionaries/ page
needs_review.finding: The Area/Regional Director query surfaced Mark Bartek (East Area Director, wife Angie), Hilary Draftz (West Area Director, husband Tim) and Greg Schmidt (former regional director, wife Elli) — all on focus.org speaker/press pages, not on per-person giving pages.
needs_review.recommendation: Not emitted: citing a speakers page as personal_page would be a false citation, and Greg Schmidt is described as a FORMER staffer. A reviewer could check whether /missionaries/ slugs exist for Bartek and Draftz; if so they are shape-2 couple pages worth two records each.

needs_review.issue: Search engine ignores negative exclusions on this domain
needs_review.finding: Two separate exclusion queries (searches 7 and 12) returned result sets identical to their unexcluded counterparts — every '-surname' term came back in the results.
needs_review.evidence: Query 'focus.org missionaries couple page -Wentworth -Lucido ...' returned Wentworth, Lucido, Connelly and Foy; query '"Family - FOCUS.org" missionaries -Hickson -Nieto ...' returned all ten excluded surnames.
needs_review.recommendation: For the next FOCUS wave, drop the '-surname' depth technique from the standing method for this target and budget those searches on qualifier rotation instead. The productive axis was the literal indexed-title suffix ('Family - FOCUS.org'), which is what exposed the surname-only and single-name-slug family pages.

needs_review.finding: Assigned budget was 18 WebSearch searches; 20 were actually issued. I lost the running count around search 13 and only caught the discrepancy when reconciling coverage[] against searches_used at write time.
needs_review.evidence: coverage[] contains 20 distinct query entries, each corresponding to one issued WebSearch call.
needs_review.recommendation: Treat searches_used=20 as the true figure for this slice when costing the wave. The last two searches (the Ohio/Texas/Arizona and Colorado/Virginia/Pennsylvania title sweeps) each returned new couple pages, so the overrun was productive, but the count is still over budget.
